summary.whatChanges: Number and bigint format checks (e.g. `.int()`, `z.int64()`) now narrow the stored minimum/maximum bounds instead of overwriting them, so bounds set by earlier `.min()`/`.max()` calls survive. Tests cover the new ordering behavior for `minValue`/`maxValue` and JSON Schema output.
behaviorChanges: z.number().min(0).max(23).int() now keeps minimum 0 / maximum 23 instead of being widened to the int32 range
toJSONSchema output for number schemas is now order-independent between .int() and .min()/.max(), emitting the tighter bounds
Format checks only tighten bag.minimum/maximum; they no longer relax previously stored tighter bounds
risks: Callers relying on the old overwrite semantics (format widening previously narrowed bounds) will see different minValue/maxValue and JSON Schema output
Bounds set by .min()/.max() applied after a format check still overwrite unconditionally, so full order-independence may not hold in the reverse direction
Bigint bounds are compared against Number.NEGATIVE_INFINITY/POSITIVE_INFINITY with casts; mixed bigint/number typing in the bag relies on loose comparison semantics
Only bag metadata changes; the format check's own runtime validation range is unchanged, so metadata and actual validation could diverge
